name: Epoch-Leviathan
geological_features: Stratified cloud layers with distinct chemical compositions
Atmospheric convection cells the size of terrestrial planets
specific_features: Massive atmospheric fauna visible from orbit
description: Epoch-Leviathan is a gas giant harboring one of the most extraordinary discoveries in exobiology: atmospheric fauna of colossal scale. The creatures drift through the stratified cloud layers, their bodies adapted to the immense pressures and wind speeds, some individuals spanning kilometers in width like living islands in the sky.

The dense atmosphere supports these beings through buoyancy and thermal convection, and the layered chemical composition provides diverse nutrient sources at different altitudes. The creatures migrate vertically through the cloud bands in slow, centuries-long cycles, following chemical gradients with an instinct honed over evolutionary timescales that dwarf most planetary histories.

The leviathans appear to be extraordinarily long-lived, with isotope analysis suggesting individual lifespans measured in millennia. They show no signs of intelligence, but their behavior patterns suggest a form of collective memory encoded in chemical signals left in the atmospheric currents they traverse.

The presence of macroscopic life in a gas giant atmosphere has rewritten textbooks on the conditions necessary for complex organisms. Helium-3 harvesting continues in the upper atmosphere above the fauna's range, but conservation protocols strictly limit operations in the inhabited cloud bands.
